conventions.convention: Batch 5 uses complete downward gradient-like fields with the exact normalized local Morse model. Batch 6 separately supplies the compactness, matching and counts for arbitrary metric Morse–Smale gradients.

Broken Morse trajectories consist of at least one nonconstant component, modulo independent component translations. Indices strictly decrease; the space is empty when the source index is no greater than the target index, including equal endpoints.

Geometric convergence of normalized Morse trajectories is uniform convergence of their height parametrizations; its equivalence with independently shifted smooth convergence is proved in the compactness theorem.

Trajectory intersections use kernel first and normal quotient second; orbit orientations remove the positive flow ray first. With outward-normal-first boundary orientation, an index-two broken endpoint has sign minus the product of its two trajectory signs.

Continuation solutions retain their time origin and are never quotiented by translation, including constant data. The datum has one fixed compact transition window and autonomous metric Morse–Smale tails.

A regular parameter family requires surjectivity of the augmented operator, rather than regularity of every vertical member. Its orientation is parameter first; the augmented rigid counting sign is minus the raw kernel sign, giving Φ⁰−Φ¹=∂⁺K+K∂⁻.

The relative handle cellular complex is the particular characteristic-disk CW model. Value-ordered handle stages need not be skeleta; an actual finite CW structure on the incoming face is supplied or constructed, rather than inferred from a homotopy model.

Naturality of the Morse–singular comparison means independence of Morse data and auxiliary choices, with orientation changes identified by diagonal generator signs. Functoriality for smooth maps is not asserted.

Local fixed-point index uses displacement id−f and is defined for n≥1. In dimension one its sphere degree is reduced degree on S⁰. The geometric index sum requires isolated fixed points; the algebraic Lefschetz number also covers nonisolated fixed sets and dimension zero.

Graph precedes diagonal in the ordered intersection. The diagonal normal coordinate is first minus second; cap is cohomology first. The dual basis satisfies evaluation of β∪α equal to the Kronecker delta, and the diagonal expansion has coefficient (−1)^p.

The derivative formula for the orientation-cover lift requires a local diffeomorphism. The two-lift identities explicitly assume a deck-commuting lift; the general nonorientable Lefschetz proof instead uses the orientation-twisted diagonal without a lifting assumption.

The Lefschetz number is the alternating rational homology trace for continuous self-maps of closed smooth manifolds, under AC. Empty manifolds give zero; dimension-zero fixed-point counting is treated separately in the fixed-point theorem.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated smooth hyperbolic invariant-axis field, sufficiently small mixed boundary data s(0)=a, u(T)=b have a unique solution staying in the prescribed ball for every T>0. The endpoint maps and all mixed coordinate derivatives have uniform exponential bounds. Substitution T=1/ρ extends both endpoint maps smoothly and flatly by zero at ρ=0.

Assume AC. A finite broken configuration of autonomous Morse–Smale metric-gradient pieces with zero or one regular continuation middle, or one augmented-regular compact family of middles with parameter-independent ends, has local geometric charts [0,δ)^N×B. Positive neck coordinates are reciprocal actual passage times; charts have inverse coverage and smooth compatible changes with positive normal derivatives. Two regular continuation windows separated by a variable autonomous plateau admit the same local matching construction, retaining the plateau parameter.

Assume AC and the stated closed Morse–Smale data, including actual metric gradients, or adapted excellent relative data. Each abstract compactified unstable manifold is a compact disk with unstable manifold as interior and the stated critical/exit boundary stratification. The characteristic disks give an actual finite unstable-cell CW structure in the closed case and a relative CW core equivalent as a pair to the cobordism in the relative case, with the incoming CW structure explicitly supplied or constructed.

Assume AC. For a connected closed smooth n-manifold, the first-minus-second normalized diagonal class with first-factor orientation coefficients has cap equal to the diagonal twisted fundamental class, expansion U=Σ(−1)^p β_{p,j}×α_{p,j}, and graph pullback evaluation L(f) for every smooth self-map. For n≥1 and nondegenerate fixed points this evaluation is the finite sum of sign det(I−Df). No orientability or lifting hypothesis on f is needed.

Assume AC and a regular continuation datum on a closed manifold. Every sequence has a geometrically convergent broken subsequence; the geometric compactification is compact, metrizable and second countable with open dense unbroken locus. Tail count is bounded by endpoint index difference; equal-index spaces are finite, and index-difference-one added configurations are exactly the two stated once-broken patterns. The proof also supplies pointed and full autonomous compactness for actual metric ends and finite rigid end counts.

Assume AC. Endpoint unstable rays orient regular continuation spaces and their rigid solutions. For index difference one, negative-tail boundary signs are the product of piece signs and positive-tail boundary signs are minus that product. The parameter-first augmented convention gives endpoint signs −τ(u⁰), +τ(u¹) and positive broken products when augmented rigid counting signs are minus raw kernel signs. Actual metric stable normal co-orientations and positive finite passage determinant blocks are also supplied.

Assume AC. For a closed Morse–Smale pair with normalized downward gradient-like field and distinct critical endpoints, every ordinary sequence has a shifted smooth broken subsequence. The height compactification is compact, metrizable and second countable with open dense ordinary stratum and length bounded by index drop. If f(p)≤f(q), both spaces are empty.

Assume AC. For a closed Morse–Smale pair with index drop two, the geometric compactification is a compact metrizable second-countable smooth one-manifold with interior the ordinary moduli space and boundary the finite disjoint union of products M(p,r)×M(r,q) over intermediate index λ(p)−1.

Assume AC and the characteristic disks of the stated closed or adapted relative Morse–Smale data. Consecutive-index cellular coefficients are trajectory counts modulo two and the signed Morse coefficients over the integers, with every displayed dimension-normalization sign equal to +1 for the specified kernel-normal, flow-first and outward-normal-first conventions. Degree one uses the chosen signed vertex generators.

Assume AC and two regular continuation data joined by a regular augmented two-parameter datum. Counting the finite augmented virtual-dimension-zero space gives degree-one K with Φ⁰−Φ¹=∂⁺K+K∂⁻. Consequently the two induced homology maps agree, and the homology continuation map depends only on the end pairs.

Assume AC. For every Morse–Smale pair on a closed smooth manifold and coefficients Z/2 or Z, the Morse–cellular–singular composite is an isomorphism independent of Morse data and auxiliary choices, with orientation independence under diagonal generator identifications. Naturality here asserts this choice independence, without asserting smooth-map functoriality.
Assume AC. Let M be a closed smooth n-manifold, n≥1, possibly disconnected or nonorientable, and let f:M→M be smooth with only isolated fixed points. Its fixed set is finite and I(f)=L(f).

A connected smooth manifold has its canonical oriented two-sheeted orientation cover. For nonempty base its deck group is Z/2; nonorientability makes the total space connected, while orientability gives two copies of the base. A closed base gives a closed cover. The empty base has empty cover and trivial deck group.

seams_checked.note: Checked adapted boundary directions and collar-extension completeness, the two-way Morse/handle correspondence, relative handle-to-core equivalence, and the finite CW-model qualification. The continuation page constructs its stronger actual characteristic-disk CW claims locally; it does not attribute them to the handle-model supplier or treat value order as skeletal order.

Checked the geometric pairing definition and the tangent-first normal Thom cap statement, including its (−1)^(rz) shuffle sign and relative-to-absolute distinction. The twisted diagonal proof accounts explicitly for normal-coordinate order and passes the integral oriented-cover calculation to rational coefficients.

Checked reduced S⁰ degree, vector-field index invariance, nondegenerate determinant signs, perturbation additivity, the boundary-degree lemma, negation, Euler finiteness and closed Poincare–Hopf. Local indices retain n≥1; the boundary-degree use does not impose or discard outwardness improperly, and tangent families explicitly require a common isolating neighbourhood.

In lem-compact-leaf-control-and-compact-ambientness-give-the-required-closedness, F6 and Proof 5.1 use the orientation-cover lemma for a closed connected smooth ambient manifold. Smoothness, canonical orientation and finite-sheeted compactness match the supplier; no derivative lift of a general self-map is invoked.

In ex-simply-connected-h-cobordisms-have-zero-whitehead-obstruction, F6 uses the connected two-sheeted orientation cover under the supposition of nonorientability, followed by triviality of connected covers of a simply connected space. For the cobordism it applies the boundaryless supplier to the interior and separately extends orientation through collars.
